topics.label: Introduction to cancer causation and lecture objectives
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer introduces the scope of the lecture on cancer causes and defines the session's key learning objectives.

topics.label: Foundations of cancer etiology, environmental risk, and epidemiology
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore the conceptual framework of cancer development as an evolutionary genetic process influenced by endogenous mutations, environmental exposures, and population-level epidemiological variations.

topics.label: Pathogens and viral mechanisms in oncogenesis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how infectious agents, illustrated in detail by the multi-factorial case of Burkitt lymphoma, drive oncogenesis.

topics.label: Molecular mechanisms of chemical and physical mutagens
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how environmental, dietary, and chemical mutagens inflict DNA damage, focusing on metabolic xenobiotic activation and DNA adduct formation.

topics.label: Tumor promotion, developmental susceptibility, and carcinogenic mechanisms
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine non-mutagenic factors in carcinogenesis, including inflammatory tumor promotion, stage-of-life cellular vulnerability, and a synthesis of DNA-damaging mechanisms.

topics.label: Methodologies for identifying and testing carcinogens
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics present the experimental, genomic, and epidemiological approaches used to identify carcinogen exposure and evaluate the carcinogenic potential of substances.

topics.label: Carcinogenic risk assessment and lecture conclusion
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer concludes the session by summarizing cancer causation and framing environmental exposures in the context of everyday risk-benefit decisions.
